title: No known SST product artifact explains the 1982-2022 east Pacific and pattern-effect gap to 31 CMIP6 models; DOISST steps put 60S-60N warming at the model median and hide 17-23% of the gap
abstract: Question: can the known step and drift artifacts in SST products (DOISST v2.1 input steps, the 2018 OI SST v2 / AMIP forcing step, the missing ship-buoy adjustment in HadISST1 and OI v2) explain any part of the difference between the observed 1982-2022 SST trend pattern and CMIP6 coupled simulations? Approach: we read ts of 112 members of 31 CMIP6 models (historical + SSP2-4.5) from the public Pangeo zarr copy with a chunk-range reader and put them on the same 60S-60N ice-free 5-degree boxes as 11 observational versions (raw, step-corrected and bias-adjusted DOISST, OI v2, HadISST1, plus ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2 and ESA CCI). We compared trends of the 60S-60N mean (Tg), the east equatorial Pacific minus 30S-30N, the west-east Pacific gradient, 50-60S, and the Green's-function pattern term P (five GFMIP models), with equal model weights. Results: all 11 versions put the east Pacific contrast (-0.135 to -0.160 C/decade; CMIP6 mean +0.020, no member below -0.126), the gradient (0.155-0.203; no member above 0.134) and P (-0.45 to -0.75 W m-2 K-1; CMIP6 mean -0.07) outside or at the edge of all models. Thus the known artifacts explain none of the discrepancy. DOISST only moves Tg to the CMIP6 median (0.171, 52nd percentile; corrected 0.130-0.137, 14th-17th; other products 0th-21st). By this dilution it hides 17-23% of the P gap (20-26% for 1982-2014), while the radiative trend of the non-uniform warming (Q) changes by less than 8%. In a 30-model relation of ECS on Tg (r = 0.68), DOISST gives 3.7 K and the corrected DOISST 2.9-3.0 K (shift +0.64 to +0.76 K). In 2001-2022 no version is outside the CMIP6 range. Limitations: only documented artifacts are tested, model ts is clipped at freezing and coastal boxes are filled, the Green's functions are linear and model-dependent, correction sizes are uncertain by up to a factor of two, and the ECS relation is a sensitivity, not a new estimate.

display.caption: 1982-2022 trend-pattern metrics: 112 CMIP6 members (grey), model means (dark), equal-weight CMIP6 mean (black line) and 11 observational versions (colour). All versions are outside CMIP6 for the east Pacific contrast and the Green's-function pattern term; only DOISST (orange) puts the 60S-60N warming rate at the CMIP6 median.

Observed minus CMIP6-mean Green's-function pattern term P for each observational version and period. DOISST (orange) has a gap 17-23% (1982-2022) and 20-26% (1982-2014) smaller than its step-corrected versions (blue). Grey band: 1 SD of CMIP6 (model spread and internal variability). In 2001-2022 the CMIP6 spread covers all versions.

CMIP6 ECS (Zelinka et al. 2020) against the 1982-2022 60S-60N SST trend of 30 models (r = 0.68). Vertical lines: observational versions. DOISST implies 3.7 K; its step-corrected versions 2.9-3.0 K; the other products 2.3-3.1 K.
